reviewer: Claude agent review (Opus), not a human historian
text: 2026-10-23: the book was rewritten to the storytelling template (README §6) and approved on an independent review (story order 01–05, 07, 06, 08–12; three names and three years in the prose), checked against the published version and its review, facts.json (44 facts, all used) and research/vijayanagara-verified.md, with all thirteen pictures opened and compared with their alt texts. The turning point is the rally and the ring at scene 9; the mercy at the river (scene 10) shows his greatness.

Earlier blockers 1, 2 and 6 to 20 stay fixed and the dignity choices hold. The introduction had brought back the 'two sons' and handover wording (blockers 4 and 5), and scene 2 and the summary an ambiguous 'previous king' for the testament (blocker 3); these now read as the older house's king, a regency until the princes came of age, the throne passing to the minister's family, and Krishna as one of the king's younger brothers.

Under the never-soften rule the prose now says the king himself imprisoned Timmarasu and his sons, and keeps Nuniz's 'he cried out that they were traitors' at the rally. The order to slay the fleeing men and the blinding stay on the evidence page under research §12, both resting on Nuniz alone and the blinding rejected by historians (1936).

The writer's disclosed choices are accepted: the dream on the Kalinga march, where the poem itself sets it; the king receiving the Kondavidu captives (he was at Amaravati fifteen days later); the Portuguese on the Mahanavami platform, where Paes seats Figueiredo's party.

Newcomer test (README §7): (1) yes, after the fixes (Kalinga glossed as Orissa, the Telugu god and Kannada king explained, Mahanavami named as the nine-day Navaratri festival, the queens' gift names moved to the evidence page, the Portuguese captain introduced, the boast at the turning point made unambiguous); (2) yes, the night of the eyes, the rally and ring and the call-back at the river carry the suspense, and the ring runs from scene 4 to the last line. Picture wishes (period dress for scenes 4 and 5; the river mercy; the ring reaching the queens) are recorded for the owner.

2026-10-15: approved on a third read of story.json (teaser, introduction, twelve scenes with paragraphs, alt texts and dramatised lists, summary, ನಿಮಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತೇ?, visitToday, provenance, disclosure, content note), facts.json (44 facts, identical to story.facts), dynasty.json and outline.md, after a first pass that returned twenty text blockers and a second pass that found one still open (the outline's 'two centuries') plus stale dramatised lines, a scene-05 contradiction and an incomplete scene-08 alt, all now fixed.

Blockers found on the first pass and fixed: (1) 'two centuries old' city in 1509, now 'more than a century and a half'; (2) Portuguese 'in Goa selling horses and guns' in 1509, now horse traders from overseas; (3) the testament credited to the previous king, now Saluva Narasimha's; (4) Krishna as Narasa's 'younger son' and 'two sons', contradicting his three brothers and Achyuta, now 'Narasa's son, Vira Narasimha's brother' and 'two of Narasa's sons'; (5) Saluva Narasimha as 'the last Saluva king' handing over the kingdom, now a regency until the princes came of age (Nuniz, disclosed); (6) Timmarasu 'twenty years beside him' and the 'twenty-year-old minister', now 'in all the campaigns that followed' and 'the old minister who had brought him up', with f-timmarasu-fate to match; (7) 'twenty years ago' for the unverified end of Saluva Narasimha's reign, dropped; (8) 'after every victory, Tirumala', now 'again and again in the years that followed' and, in the summary, the kanakabhisheka after Udayagiri; (9) 'a year earlier' for the 17 months since February 1513, now a year and a half; (10) the Vijayanagara flag on Udayagiri's walls, against the bible, now soldiers and horse-tail standards; (11) the king drawing back and nobody crossing, against Nuniz, now the Gajapati giving no reply and the crossing fought on both sides; (12) source commentary inside scenes ('a foreigner later wrote', 'an eyewitness wrote it down', 'the chronicler's count', 'the stones of 1524 wrote', 'nobody knows where the ring went'), now told as events; (13) the king on horseback at the rally, now standing until he mounts after giving the ring (the image's mounted rally is disclosed); (14) Vyasatirtha's 1524 houses as the king's gift inside the 1520 festival, now 'received many gifts from the king; in 1524 houses at Tirumala, and by the king's order a share of the gift'; (15) Nuniz's della Ponte, lime and tax remission credited to Paes, now credited to Nuniz and told as narration; (16) 'having given up hope of living', now 'knowing the end was near'; (17) 'the story of Goda Devi', not in the verified research, dropped; (18) alt texts naming eyes, goat, blood and god by negation, removed; (19) the Aravidu kings 'more than seventy years', now 'some seventy'; (20) two broken Commons category links, now Bala_Krishna_Temple_(Hampi) and Kondavid_Fort.

Every name, number, year, relationship and quotation was compared with research/vijayanagara-verified.md, with Nuniz re-read in Sewell (Project Gutenberg 3310) for the river crossing, the Raichur rally and the son's death: the Tuluva pedigree and the Rama-Lakshmana verse; Narasa's death in Saka 1424; the accession legend (Nuniz alone, framed as the capital's story by the owner's decision); 22 to 26 July 1509; Magha su. 14 of the Sukla year and the coronation gifts and birudas; Chandragiri and the year and a half; Ummattur, Sivasamudram, Srirangapatna, 22 September 1512; Udayagiri 9 June 1514, the aunt, the 26 days, the gold bath of 30,000 varahas; Balakrishna 'with great care', 16 February 1515, nine villages; Kondavidu 23 June 1515, Virabhadra and the Patra-Samantas spared, a governor by October; Amaravati 8 July 1515 with Chinnadevi's Ratnadhenu and Tirumaladevi's Saptasagara; the two-league offer; the Potnuru pillar; the marriage for peace and the lands returned; the Srikakulam dream and 'ನಾನು ತೆಲುಗು ರಾಯ, ಓ ಕನ್ನಡ ರಾಯ'; the dharma verses 204, 205 and 285; Peddana, Nandi Timmana, Timmanna's Kannada Bharata, Vasantotsava, Sahiti-samarangana-sarvabhauma; Cide Mercar and the horse trade; Raichur on 19 May 1520 as Sewell's reckoning, the rally, the ring, the charge, the compassion at the river, the released women, sixteen thousand dead; Figueiredo's twenty musketeers, twenty days after the battle, persons and property spared, 'one good man', looting stopped; the month's wait, the price of peace, Mudgal, Bijapur, the Bahmani princes at Gulbarga; Paes's person, routine, audience, Rome, Lisbon, Nagalapura and the tank, the Mahanavami and the review after the festival; the Tirumala bronzes c. 1517 with names on the shoulders, the seventh visit and the jewelled kullayi; the son born 1518 and 'ruling the earth' in Saka 1446; the last ride, Belgaum, the will naming Achyuta with the son of eighteen months; 2 April 1528, 23 April 1529 as one of his last gifts; death in 1529 at about forty-two (from the 1487 tradition); Hampi World Heritage Site 1986.

Dignity and the storytelling rule: the king is calm, unafraid, merciful and never fat, cruel or in despair; Paes's 'rather fat', small-pox and rage, Nuniz's order to slay the fleeing men, the sati purpose of the ring, the dam beheadings, the daily sacrifices, Salabat Khan's execution and Timmarasu's blinding are kept to the facts and the last page; the Adil Shah and the Gajapati are never insulted; Chinnadevi and Tirumaladevi are always queens. Inside scenes events happen in order and with confidence; the two framings kept ('the story the capital told', 'as he himself later wrote') are for the Nuniz-only legend and the literary dream. Every invention, choice of telling and present-day geography is listed in its scene's dramatised list.

Kannada and data: NFC; no em dash; Kannada digits only in Kannada prose; ZWNJ only after a virama; names consistent (ತಿಮ್ಮರಸು, ಸಾಳುವ ತಿಮ್ಮ, ಪಾಯಿಸ್, ಫೆರ್ನಾವೊ ನೂನಿಜ್, ಚಿನ್ನಾದೇವಿ, ತಿರುಮಲಾದೇವಿ, ಫಿಗೈರೆಡೊ, ಆದಿಲ್ ಶಾಹ, ಹಂಪೆ); loanwords replaced (ಹರದಾರಿ, ಹದ್ದು, ರಾಜ್ಯಪಾಲ, ಒಂದು ಬಟ್ಟಲು). Every scene and didYouKnow id resolves and every fact is used. The Vijayanagara dynasty entry agrees with research section 10 (Harihara I c. 1336 to c. 1355, Bukka I joint from 1346 and died Saka 1298, Harihara II 1377 to 1404, Deva Raya II 1424 to 1446, Saluva Narasimha from c. 1486, Vira Narasimha 1503 to 1509, Krishnadevaraya 1509 to 1529, Achyuta 1529 to 1542, Sadasiva 1542 to c. 1570 with Talikota on 23 January 1565, Venkatapati Raya 1586 to 1614), with the 1336/1346, Vidyaranya, Aravidu-start and 1646 caveats in the dating note and kn/en aligned. Provenance links were checked against the archive.org metadata API, Commons, te.wikisource, Wikidata and Gutenberg.
illustrations: All thirteen WebPs (cover, scene-01 to scene-12, 1600x900, each under 200 KB) were opened and compared with scene text, alt and bible/style.md, with enlarged crops of faces, headgear, banners, towers, dress and the bronzes. Five were regenerated after the second pass: scene-02 (maroon banners with a gold sun-disc emblem), scene-03 (emblem banners and pennants where the text has horse-tail standards; its prompt had asked for 'Vijayanagara banners'), scene-04 (queens in modern saris with stitched blouses and bridal tiaras), scene-08 (drum towers rendered with clock faces and a striped modern-looking flag) and scene-12 (both queen bronzes bare-breasted, against the real bronze and the prompt, and a smooth crown-like cap). The replacements show a flat golden lotus and no emblem banners; horse-tail standards on Udayagiri's walls; the queens in period breast-cloths, covered and dignified; timber platforms carrying kettledrums and plain pennants; and the queens' bronzes fully draped with the king's ribbed kullayi.

The king is the same man throughout: a smooth oval clean-shaven face, slim strong build, the tall ribbed kullayi at court and a gilded helmet on campaign (cover, 01 to 06, 08 to 11), bare-chested at the temple as on the bronze (04, 05); scene-07 shows him with the cap set aside and reads slightly older. He is handsome, calm and never fat. Timmarasu is consistent: an older lean Brahmin with a short white moustache and a plain kullayi (01, 02, 05, 08, 10). The queens appear as queens in public acts (04, 05, 12), at Amaravati holding the golden cow of the Ratnadhenu and a vessel for the Saptasagara gift. There are no eyes, no goat, no blood in close-up, no beheadings, no sacrifice and no god in the dream scene.

Nits recorded and not regenerated: scene-02's background gopura under scaffolding has a reddish plastered surface; scene-04's queens wear centre-parted hair with jasmine rather than high hair-knots; scene-05's queens wear stitched blouses and the gold includes modern-looking ingots; scene-10's Portuguese wear crested morions, a few decades later than 1520, Figueiredo has a small frilled collar, and plain yellow banners hang on Raichur's walls; scene-09 shows plain pennants on both sides and the rally mounted (disclosed); scene-11 shows about fifteen horses where Paes counts eleven; the scene-12 king's face is idol-like rather than portrait-like.
limitations: This is an AI review by a Claude agent; no human historian, epigraphist or Telugu scholar has read the text or checked the images.

Fact checking was limited to research/vijayanagara-verified.md and its named editions (Sewell 1900 with Paes and Nuniz, EI I and IV, ASR 1907-08, 1908-09 and 1911-12, TTD 1930, EC VI, Longhurst 1917, Amuktamalyada on te.wikisource, Chenchiah 1928 and the 1936 volume as reference); Nuniz was re-read in Sewell for three passages, other primary texts were not re-fetched. The Hampi Krishna-temple records, the Amaravati record's location, the Potnuru pillar text, Saluva Narasimha's last year, the 1646 end of the dynasty, the Vellore date and the coin legend remain unverified, as the research file says.

The accession legend and much of the Raichur campaign rest on Nuniz alone, written about 1535 from hearsay at the capital; Raichur's year is disputed (Sewell 1520, Ferishta 1521, Nuniz 1522); the Hazara Rama attribution and the origin of Nagalapura's name are disputed. The book tells one reading and the facts carry the disputes.

No portrait of the king survives apart from the Tirumala bronze, which the images follow; the faces of the queens, Timmarasu, Figueiredo and Paes, the camps, temples in construction and the 1520 city are reconstructions, as the disclosure says. Images were judged at 1600x900 with enlarged crops; small distant details could not all be verified, and the nits above remain.
